course.title: Azure — Complete Cloud Engineering Course
course.description: A Azure-specific, beginner-to-advanced cloud engineering course covering identity, networking, compute, storage, databases, APIs, containers/serverless, observability, security, CI/CD, reliability and a production learning-platform capstone.
course.curriculumPolicy: Module and lesson counts are determined by the cloud concepts required to learn the platform properly; no fixed cross-cloud template is imposed.
learningOutcomes: Design secure cloud networks and identities.
Plan backup, recovery and failure handling.

modules.title: Cloud & Azure Foundations
modules.description: Cloud models, Azure regions, availability zones, subscriptions, resource groups and management hierarchy.

lessons.title: Cloud & Azure Foundations
lessons.description: Cloud models, Azure regions, availability zones, subscriptions, resource groups and management hierarchy.
learningObjectives: Understand Cloud & Azure Foundations.
Explain how the Azure service fits into an application.
Apply secure and production-oriented configuration.
Reason about scalability, reliability and cost.
Complete a realistic cloud engineering task.

notes.text: Cloud models, Azure regions, availability zones, subscriptions, resource groups and management hierarchy.

This lesson explains cloud & azure foundations from a practical cloud-engineering perspective. First understand the problem, then the cloud service, then how the service fits into a real application. The goal is not to memorize console buttons; the student should understand the architecture and the reason behind each choice.
Why This Matters in a Real Website

A production learning platform needs secure identity, reliable infrastructure, scalable storage, controlled networking and observable services. Cloud & Azure Foundations is one part of that larger system.

notes.alt: Azure Cloud & Azure Foundations architecture diagram
notes.caption: Add an educational architecture diagram showing how Cloud & Azure Foundations fits into a real Azure application.

items: Understand the service/problem before choosing an implementation.
Know the important resource relationships and boundaries.
Understand security and least-privilege implications.
Understand cost, scaling and failure behavior.
Know how the feature connects to the application backend.

notes.code:
Requirement: Design an Azure architecture for a learning platform and map resources to resource groups.

Architecture: define the resources, network boundaries, identity, data flow and monitoring needed for the solution.

Implementation: choose the appropriate managed service configuration and document the important decisions.

notes.text: How to Think About the Example

items: Identify the application requirement.
Identify the cloud resources involved.
Identify who or what is allowed to access them.
Identify what happens when traffic or data grows.
Identify what happens if a component fails.
Identify what should be monitored and what it will cost.
Giving broad permissions instead of least privilege.
Putting every resource in a public network.
Ignoring backups and recovery testing.
Choosing a managed service without understanding its limits and cost.
Deploying without logs, metrics and health checks.
Use infrastructure and configuration that can be reproduced.
Keep secrets outside source code.
Prefer private networking for databases and internal services.
Use least-privilege identities.
Monitor important user-facing and infrastructure signals.
Design failure and rollback paths before production.
I can explain Cloud & Azure Foundations in my own words.
I can draw the architecture without looking at the notes.
I can identify the security boundary.
I can explain one scaling and one failure scenario.
I can estimate which parts could create operational cost.

practicals.title: Guided Practical — Cloud & Azure Foundations
practicals.objective: Apply Cloud & Azure Foundations using a realistic Azure scenario.
steps: Document how the component would be operated in production.
practicals.starterCode:
# Practical architecture for Azure — Cloud & Azure Foundations
# Requirement: Design an Azure architecture for a learning platform and map resources to resource groups.
practicals.expectedOutput: A working or clearly documented Azure implementation/architecture demonstrating Cloud & Azure Foundations.

tasks.title: Dedicated Task — Cloud & Azure Foundations
tasks.description: Design an Azure architecture for a learning platform and map resources to resource groups.
requirements: Use Azure appropriately for Cloud & Azure Foundations.
Document the architecture and data flow.
acceptanceCriteria: Architecture is understandable without verbal explanation.
Resources and dependencies are clearly identified.
Security boundaries are documented.
Normal and failure behavior are tested or demonstrated.
Operational considerations are documented.

quiz.question: What is the primary learning goal of Cloud & Azure Foundations?
options: Understand and apply Cloud & Azure Foundations in Azure.
quiz.answer: Understand and apply Cloud & Azure Foundations in Azure.
quiz.explanation: The lesson connects Cloud & Azure Foundations to real cloud architecture and operations.

quiz.question: Which production concern should be considered alongside functionality?
quiz.answer: Security, reliability, scaling and cost
quiz.explanation: Cloud architecture must consider operational behavior, not only whether the feature works.
